questions.questionText: Why don't fully-connected layers scale well to raw images?
options: Images can't be represented as numbers
A modest-sized image has hundreds of thousands of pixels, requiring an enormous number of weights, and treats every pixel as independent, ignoring spatial structure
Fully-connected layers can only process grayscale images
There is no real problem, CNNs offer no advantage
questions.correctAnswer: A modest-sized image has hundreds of thousands of pixels, requiring an enormous number of weights, and treats every pixel as independent, ignoring spatial structure
questions.explanation: Both the parameter explosion and the loss of spatial relationships between nearby pixels make fully-connected layers a poor fit for raw image input.

questions.questionText: What is "parameter sharing" in a convolutional layer?
options: Multiple filters share the exact same weights as each other
The same filter's weights are reused at every position across the image, rather than learning separate weights per pixel location
Parameters are shared between the training and test sets
It refers to sharing a model between multiple users
questions.correctAnswer: The same filter's weights are reused at every position across the image, rather than learning separate weights per pixel location
questions.explanation: Applying the same small filter everywhere is what makes convolution dramatically more parameter-efficient than a fully-connected layer, and gives translation invariance for free.

questions.questionText: What does a pooling layer (e.g. max pooling) do?
options: It downsamples the feature map (e.g. keeping only the max value in each small block), reducing size and adding some translation invariance
It converts the image to grayscale
It replaces the need for an activation function
questions.correctAnswer: It downsamples the feature map (e.g. keeping only the max value in each small block), reducing size and adding some translation invariance
questions.explanation: Pooling shrinks feature maps to reduce computation for subsequent layers, while also making the network somewhat robust to small shifts in where a feature appears.
